title: Trade in Minutes! Rationality-Driven Agentic System for Quantitative Financial Trading

task.value: Building a rationality-driven multi-agent LLM system that develops and optimizes programmatic trading bots offline and deploys them for minute-level quantitative trading in stock index futures and crypto markets.
task.quote: we present TiMi (Trade in Minutes), a rationality-driven multi-agent system that architecturally decouples strategy development from minute-level deployment.

architecture.value: Four agents: macro analysis agent (strategies from technical indicators), strategy adaptation agent (pair-specific rules/parameters), bot evolution agent (writes layered code bots), feedback reflection agent (linear-programming parameter solving); policy, optimization, deployment stages; CPU-only bot deployment.
architecture.quote: (1) policy stage — complex reasoning and strategy development occur in an offline environment, fully leveraging the capabilities of specialized agents, including actions of \mathcal{A}_{\text{ma}} , \mathcal{A}_{\text{sa}} , and \mathcal{A}_{\text{be}} to generate prototype trading bots

data.value: Market technical indicators (volume, amplitude, K-lines, funding rates) for 213 trading pairs in U.S. stock index futures (CME) and mainstream/altcoin crypto futures (Binance), minute-level frequency.
data.quote: We select top-tier exchanges with high liquidity, i.e., CME for stock index futures and Binance for cryptocurrencies.

window.value: Backtesting on 2024 historical data; live trading from January to April 2025. Progressive validation: historical development, real-time simulation, then live trading.
window.quote: Table 3: Live trading comparison of mainstream methods across U.S. stock index futures and cryptocurrency markets from 2025 January to April.

models.value: DeepSeek-V3 for semantic analysis, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct for code programming, DeepSeek-R1 for mathematical reasoning.
models.quote: We strategically adopt DeepSeek-V3 for semantic analysis, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct for code programming, and DeepSeek-R1 for mathematical reasoning.

baselines.value: Quantitative: MACD, momentum, grid, pairs trading, ETF&PCA, TSMOM, OFI; ML&RL: LSTM, Autoformer, PatchTST, DQN, DDPG; LLM agents: FinGPT, FinMem, TradingAgents.
baselines.quote: Baselines. We compare TiMi against three representative categories: (1) quantitative methods, including MACD (Wang & Kim, 2018) optimized by historical volatility, momentum strategy (Jegadeesh & Titman, 1993), grid trading (Griffin et al., 2003)

headline_result.value: Live trading (Jan–Apr 2025): ARR 6.4%, 8.0%, 13.7% on U.S. stock index futures, mainstream coins, altcoins; SR 0.74, 0.79, 0.86; MDD 20.3%, 25.1%, 32.8%; 213 pairs.

costs.value: Models order fees and periodic funding rates; LIMIT orders for entry to get maker fees and avoid entry slippage; funding-rate-based order reduction; pre-trade price deviation check. Deployment end-to-end latency avg 137 ms.
costs.quote: We model and mitigate two primary costs: order fees and periodic funding rates. TiMi employs LIMIT orders for entry to capture favorable maker fees and eliminate entry slippage.

uncertainty.value: Cross-pair return dispersion reported (σ = 11.03% for TiMi vs 29.64% for DDPG); latency std dev and P99. No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported.
uncertainty.quote: TiMi exhibits markedly performance stability with reduced variance ( \sigma = 11.03%) and rare tail events ( < 2%), indicating more consistent returns over market dynamics compared to alternatives.

leakage_controls.value: Live trading evaluation in 2025 after development on historical data; authors note LLM-agent baselines may exploit posterior information in backtests. No explicit contamination control described.
leakage_controls.quote: We implement a progressive validation: initial strategy development using historical data, followed by trading simulation with real-time market data, and culminating in live trading evaluation.

limitations.value: Need for an optimization stage limits zero-shot performance when porting to new markets; broader concerns about market dynamics, liquidity, fairness and institutional-retail gap.
limitations.quote: The necessity of the optimization stage limits the zero-shot performance of trading bots developed by TiMi when porting to new markets.

release.value: Authors promise to open-source deployment implementation and release corner case list; no location given.
release.quote: Crucially, we will open-source the implementation of TiMi product for deployment and release the key corner case list (from both back simulation and live deployment).
